annotation_provenance.source: Lab worklog (Google Doc "Work Log"), mirrored partially in /Users/prakx/project_dir/RA/3d-genome-worklog

data.required: Matched short-read (Illumina, HCT116) and long-read (ONT, HCT116) RNA-seq

code.notes: Public GitHub repo, buildable, demo (run_sample.sh) works out of the box.

environment.required: Python 3.6 pinned env (numpy, pandas, scipy, intervaltree, pysam, htslib) plus a separate R env for the TPM-generation script
environment.notes: Buildable but brittle: old version pins caused repeated compiler/dependency conflicts, and the R 3.6 environment silently corrupted the TPM script by auto-converting a text column to a factor.

model_checkpoints.required: None — EM-based method, no pretrained model

parameters.required: Exact RepeatMasker-derived TE GTF (filtering/processing criteria) used to produce the paper's 97,746 quantified TEs
parameters.notes: Paper states only "created using RepeatMasker for GRCh38 [ref 27]". The GitHub repo, Zenodo archive, and Figshare dataset only include a tiny demo GTF (1-2KB) or a HERV-only annotation — never the genome-wide file actually used. Ref 27 (obtained via RIT library request) provided no additional processing detail either.

blockers.description: The exact TE annotation GTF (and its filtering criteria) used to generate the paper's headline correlation figure was never released and could not be reconstructed — the paper's own cited reference for it contains no further detail.
R 3.6's default factor-conversion of text columns silently broke the TPM-generation script (preprocessing_ONT.R); required rebuilding the R environment from scratch to diagnose.
Outdated/brittle dependency pins (Python 3.6, old compiler requirements) cost roughly 2-3 weeks of environment setup before any data could be processed.

per_result_analysis.result: Demo dataset (20-locus annotation bundled in repo)
per_result_analysis.notes: Pipeline ran end-to-end, EM converged, output files matched expected structure.
TP=3367, TN=4425, FP=116, FN=125 — PI confirmed this "closely matches the expected behavior reported in the paper."

per_result_analysis.result: Fig. 3G-equivalent: short-read vs. long-read TE quantification correlation, full genome-wide RepeatMasker annotation (paper reports R²≈0.9)
per_result_analysis.notes: 701,488 TEs compared; recall 0.994 (near-perfect detection) but Spearman R² = -0.024. Detection works; quantitative correlation does not, and the gap tracks the missing-GTF blocker above rather than a pipeline defect.
Spearman R² improved to 0.087, then to 0.202 with weighted simulated data — still far short of the paper's ~0.9, but confirms the young-TE subset behaves better, as the paper claims qualitatively.

scoring_rubric_v0.1.notes: Scored out of the blueprint's 100-point rubric (weights: 20/20/15/15/10/10/10). The single largest deduction is parameters_configuration — the undocumented TE-GTF construction is the load-bearing gap.

verified_reproduction.summary: Structural reproduction succeeded: the EM pipeline builds, runs end-to-end, converges, and produces sane output on multiple TE annotations, with detection recall consistently >0.96. Quantitative reproduction of the paper's flagship correlation (R²≈0.9) was never achieved across four distinct annotation strategies tried over ~4 months (best: R²=0.202). Root cause: the exact TE annotation GTF used for the published figure was never released and its construction criteria were undocumented even in the paper's own cited methodological reference.
